## Table of Contents

- [Installation](#installation)
- [How to use Tokei](#how-to-use-tokei)

- [Common Issues](#common-issues)
- [Copyright and License](#copyright-and-license)

## Features

- Tokei is **very fast**, and is able to count millions of lines of code in seconds.

- Tokei is **accurate**, Tokei correctly handles multi line comments,
  nested comments, and not counting comments that are in strings. Providing an
  accurate code statistics.

- Tokei has huge range of languages, supporting over **150** languages, and
  their various extensions.

- Tokei can output in multiple formats (**CBOR**, **JSON**, **YAML**)
  allowing Tokei's output to be easily stored, and reused. These can also be
  reused in tokei combining a previous run's statistics with another set.

- Tokei is available on **Mac**, **Linux**, and **Windows**.

- Tokei comes with and without color. Set the env variable NO_COLOR to 1, and
  it'll be black and white.

## Installation

### Package Managers

#### Unix
```console
# Alpine Linux (since 3.13)
apk add tokei
# Arch Linux
pacman -S tokei
# Conda
conda install -c conda-forge tokei
# Fedora
sudo dnf install tokei
# FreeBSD
pkg install tokei
# NetBSD
pkgin install tokei
# Nix/NixOS
nix-env -i tokei
# OpenSUSE
sudo zypper install tokei
# Void Linux
sudo xbps-install tokei
```

#### macOS
```console
# Homebrew
brew install tokei
# MacPorts
sudo port selfupdate
sudo port install tokei
```

#### Windows
```console
# Winget
winget install XAMPPRocky.tokei
# Scoop
scoop install tokei
```

### Manual

You can download prebuilt binaries in the releases section.

## How to use Tokei

#### Basic usage

This is the basic way to use tokei. Which will report on the code in `./foo`
and all subfolders.

```shell
$ tokei ./foo
```

#### Multiple folders
To have tokei report on multiple folders in the same call, simply add all the
folders you'd like tokei to examine.

```shell
$ tokei ./foo ./bar ./baz
```

#### Excluding folders
Tokei will respect all `.gitignore` and `.ignore` files, and you can use
the `--exclude` option to exclude any additional files. The `--exclude` flag has
the same semantics as `.gitignore`.

```shell
$ tokei ./foo --exclude *.rs
```

Paths to exclude can also be listed in a `.tokeignore` file, using the same
syntax as .gitignore files.

#### Sorting output
By default tokei sorts alphabetically by language name, however using `--sort`
tokei can also sort by any of the columns.

`blanks, code, comments, lines`

```shell
$ tokei ./foo --sort code
```

#### Outputting file statistics
By default tokei only outputs the total of the languages, and using `--files`
flag tokei can also output individual file statistics.

```shell
$ tokei ./foo --files
```

#### Outputting into different formats
Tokei normally outputs into a nice human readable format designed for terminals.
There is also using the `--output` option various other formats that are more
useful for bringing the data into another program.

**Currently supported formats**
- JSON `--output json`
- YAML `--o

## Options

```
USAGE:
    tokei [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] [--] [input]...

FLAGS:
    -f, --files               Will print out statistics on individual files.
    -h, --help                Prints help information
        --hidden              Count hidden files.
    -l, --languages           Prints out supported languages and their extensions.
        --no-ignore           Don't respect ignore files (.gitignore, .ignore, etc.). This implies --no-ignore-parent,

## Features

- Tokei is **very fast**, and is able to count millions of lines of code in seconds.

- Tokei is **accurate**, Tokei correctly handles multi line comments,
  nested comments, and not counting comments that are in strings. Providing an
  accurate code statistics.

- Tokei has huge range of languages, supporting over **150** languages, and
  their various extensions.

- Tokei can output in multiple formats (**CBOR**, **JSON**, **YAML**)
  allowing Tokei's output to be easily stored, and reused. These can also be
  reused in tokei combining a previous run's statistics with another set.

- Tokei is available on **Mac**, **Linux**, and **Windows**.

- Tokei comes with and without color. Set the env variable NO_COLOR to 1, and
  it'll be black and white.

## Installation

### Package Managers

#### Unix
```console
# Alpine Linux (since 3.13)
apk add tokei
# Arch Linux
pacman -S tokei
# Conda
conda install -c conda-forge tokei
# Fedora
sudo dnf install tokei
# FreeBSD
pkg install tokei
# NetBSD
pkgin install tokei
# Nix/NixOS
nix-env -i tokei
# OpenSUSE
sudo zypper install tokei
# Void Linux
sudo xbps-install tokei
```

#### macOS
```console
# Homebrew
brew install tokei
# MacPorts
sudo port selfupdate
sudo port install tokei
```

#### Windows
```console
# Winget
winget install XAMPPRocky.tokei
# Scoop
scoop install tokei
```

### Manual

You can download prebuilt binaries in the releases section.

## How to use Tokei

#### Basic usage

This is the basic way to use tokei. Which will report on the code in `./foo`
and all subfolders.

```shell
$ tokei ./foo
```

#### Multiple folders
To have tokei report on multiple folders in the same call, simply add all the
folders you'd like tokei to examine.

```shell
$ tokei ./foo ./bar ./baz
```

#### Excluding folders
Tokei will respect all `.gitignore` and `.ignore` files, and you can use
the `--exclude` option to exclude any additional files. The `--exclude` flag has
the same semantics as `.gitignore`.

```shell
$ tokei ./foo --exclude *.rs
```

Paths to exclude can also be listed in a `.tokeignore` file, using the same
syntax as .gitignore files.

#### Sorting output
By default tokei sorts alphabetically by language name, however using `--sort`
tokei can also sort by any of the columns.

`blanks, code, comments, lines`

```shell
$ tokei ./foo --sort code
```

#### Outputting file statistics
By default tokei only outputs the total of the languages, and using `--files`
flag tokei can also output individual file statistics.

```shell
$ tokei ./foo --files
```

#### Outputting into different formats
Tokei normally outputs into a nice human readable format designed for terminals.
There is also using the `--output` option various other formats that are more
useful for bringing the data into another program.

**Currently supported formats**
- JSON `--output json`
- YAML `--o

value to the option, or from stdin.

```shell

```

# This is different from case 2 and 3...

# A line is COMMENT if all code content is surrounded by block comments (or there is no code)

# '/* comment */ let x = 1;' -> nothing before first, 'let x = 1' after last -> CODE ✓

print("Theory: CODE if code before first comment OR code after last comment")
print("This matches all observed cases!")

package main

// CommentStyle defines how comments work in a language
type CommentStyle struct {
	Single    []string // single-line comment prefixes
	MultiOpen []string // multi-line comment start markers
	MultiClose []string // multi-line comment end markers
	NestedComments bool // whether nested block comments are supported
}

// Language defines a programming language and its properties
type Language struct {
	Name     string
	Extensions []string
	Comment  CommentStyle
	HasChildren bool // can have embedded languages (like Markdown)
	// Some languages are identified by filename, not extension
	Filenames []string
}

// childLanguagePatterns maps parent languages to their child detection patterns
// e.g., Markdown can contain code blocks
var childLanguagePatterns = map[string]bool{
	"Markdown": true,
	"Rust":     true, // via doc comments ///
}

var cStyle = CommentStyle{
	Single:    []string{"//"},
	MultiOpen: []string{"/*"},
	MultiClose: []string{"*/"},
}

var hashStyle = CommentStyle{
	Single: []string{"#"},
}

var pythonStyle = CommentStyle{
	Single: []string{"#"},
	// Python triple-quotes are NOT comments in tokei's counting
}

var htmlStyle = CommentStyle{
	MultiOpen: []string{"<!--"},
	MultiClose: []string{"-->"},
}

var luaStyle = CommentStyle{
	Single: []string{"--"},
	MultiOpen: []string{"--[["},
	MultiClose: []string{"]]"},
}

var haskellStyle = CommentStyle{
	Single: []string{"--"},
	MultiOpen: []string{"{-"},
	MultiClose: []string{"-}"},
	NestedComments: true,
}

var rustStyle = CommentStyle{
	Single: []string{"//"},
	MultiOpen: []string{"/*"},
	MultiClose: []string{"*/"},
	NestedComments: true,
}

var sqlStyle = CommentStyle{
	Single: []string{"--"},
	MultiOpen: []string{"/*"},
	MultiClose: []string{"*/"},
}

var rubyStyle = CommentStyle{
	Single: []string{"#"},
	MultiOpen: []string{"=begin"},

# The implementation is going to be complex. Let me rethink the approach.
# Given the complexity and the fact that I need to implement:
# 1. Complex language comment parsing (hundreds of languages)
# 2. Gitignore-like pattern matching
# 3. Embedded languages (Markdown containing code blocks, Rust doc comments)
# 4. Complex output formatting
# 5. All CLI options
#
# Let me take a more pragmatic approach and write a single comprehensive Go file
# that covers all the core functionality.

# Let me first check what the exact output for the languages command looks like
# to understand all the data I need

./executable --languages 2>&1 | grep "┃ " | grep -v "Language\|━" | python3 -c "
import sys, re

data = sys.stdin.read()
for line in data.split('\n'):
    line = line.strip()
    if not line.startswith('┃') or not line.endswith('┃'):
        continue
    content = line[1:-1].strip()
    if not content:
        continue
    # Find the gap between name and extensions
    # Name is left part, extensions is right part
    # They're separated by multiple spaces
    parts = re.split(r'  {2,}', content)
    parts = [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]
    if len(parts) >= 2:
        name = parts[0]
        exts = parts[-1]
        print(f'{name!r}: {exts!r}')
    elif len(parts) == 1:
        print(f'{parts[0]!r}: <None>')
" | wc -l

import subprocess, os

# Test filename detection (not extension)
os.makedirs('/tmp/fn_test', exist_ok=True)
for fname in ['Makefile', 'makefile', 'GNUmakefile', 'Dockerfile', 'CMakeLists.txt', 
              'Gemfile', 'Rakefile', 'justfile', 'Justfile', '.justfile',
              'SConstruct', 'SConscript']:
    fpath = f'/tmp/fn_test/{fname}'
    with open(fpath, 'w') as f: f.write('test\n')
    result = subprocess.run(['./executable', fpath], capture_output=True, text=True)
    lines = result.stdout.split('\n')
    lang = next((l.strip().split()[0] for l in lines if l.strip() and not l.startswith('━') and 'Language' not in l and 'Total' not in l), 'Unknown')
    print(f'{fname} -> {lang}')
EOF

print(f'Total languages: {len(langs)}')

# ABNF, AWK, ABAP, ActionScript, Ada, Agda, Alex, Alloy, APL, Arduino C++, Ark TypeScript, Arturo, AsciiDoc, ASN.1, ASP, ASP.NET, Assembly, GNU Style Assembly, Astro, ATS, AutoHotKey, Autoconf, Autoit, Automake, AXAML
# Sorted alphabetically (case-insensitive): ABAP, ABNF, ActionScript, Ada, Agda, Alex, Alloy, APL...
# But actual: ABNF, AWK, ABAP, ActionScript...
# Hmm not quite alphabetical

# Wait: ABAP comes before ABNF in true alphabetical order, but ABNF comes first

# Sorted: ABAP (A,B,A,P) then ABNF (A,B,N,F)?

# But output shows ABNF first!

# Let me look more carefully at the sort order

mismatches = []
for i, (actual, expected) in enumerate(zip(names, sorted_names)):
    if actual != expected:
        mismatches.append((i, actual, expected))
print(f'Mismatches: {len(mismatches)}')
for i, actual, expected in mismatches[:5]:
    print(f'  {i}: actual={actual!r}, expected={expected!r}')

# I'll implement the classifyLine logic in Python and test each line

def classify_line_go(line):
    """Implement the tokei classifyLine algorithm for Go (C-style comments)"""
    # C-style: // single, /* */ multi
    
    single = ['//']
    ml_open = ['/*']
    ml_close = ['*/']
    nested = False
    
    trimmed = line.strip()
    if not trimmed:
        return 'blank'
    
    # Parse line
    first_comment_start = len(line)
    last_ml_close = -1
    has_sl_after_ml = False
    
    i = 0
    in_ml = 0
    
    while i < len(line):
        if in_ml > 0:
            # Check close
            closed = False
            for close in ml_close:
                if line[i:i+len(close)] == close:
                    in_ml -= 1
                    if in_ml == 0:
                        last_ml_close = i + len(close)
                    i += len(close)
                    closed = True
                    break
            if closed:
                continue
            # Check nested open (not for Go)
            i += 1
            continue
        
        # OUT state
        # Check ML open
        found = False
        for open_tok in ml_open:
            if line[i:i+len(open_tok)] == open_tok:
                if i < first_comment_start:
                    first_comment_start = i
                in_ml += 1
                i += len(open_tok)
                found = True
                break
        if found:
            continue
        
        # Check SL
        for sl in single:
            if line[i:i+len(sl)] == sl:
                if i < first_comment_start:
                    first_comment_start = i
                if last_ml_close >= 0:
                    has_sl_after_ml = True
                i = len(line)
                found = True
                break
        if found:
            break
        
        i += 1
    
    # Check code before first comment
    code_before = any(c not in ' \t\r' for c in line[:first_comment_start])
    if code_before:
        return 'code'
    
    # Check after last ML close
    if last_ml_close >= 0:
        after = any(c not in ' \t\r' for c in line[last_ml_close:])
        if after:
            return 'code'
        if has_sl_after_ml:
            return 'code'
        return 'comment'
    
    if first_comment_start < len(line):
        return 'comment'
    
    return 'blank'

# Read languages.go and classify each line
with open('/workspace/src/languages.go') as f:
    lines = f.readlines()

print('Lines classified as comments by my algorithm:')
for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
    classification = classify_line_go(line.rstrip('\n'))
    if classification == 'comment':
        print(f'  Line {i}: {repr(line.rstrip()[:80])}')
EOF

# in parallel and outputs as they complete. The test will likely not do exact diff
# on streaming output - it's inherently non-deterministic.

# (just different ordering) compared to original

import subprocess

                      capture_output=True, text=True)
mine = subprocess.run(['/workspace/tokei', '/tmp/testdir', '--streaming', 'simple'],
                      capture_output=True, text=True)

# Extract data rows (skip header)
orig_data = set(line.strip() for line in orig.stdout.split('\n')[2:] if line.strip())
mine_data = set(line.strip() for line in mine.stdout.split('\n')[2:] if line.strip())

print(f'Orig data: {orig_data}')
print(f'Mine data: {mine_data}')
print(f'Same: {orig_data == mine_data}')

print("testdir json - checking content:")
orig_j = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', '/tmp/testdir', '--streaming', 'json'],
                        capture_output=True, text=True)
mine_j = subprocess.run(['/workspace/tokei', '/tmp/testdir', '--streaming', 'json'],
                        capture_output=True, text=True)
import json
orig_jdata = set(json.dumps(json.loads(l), sort_keys=True) for l in orig_j.stdout.split('\n') if l.strip())
mine_jdata = set(json.dumps(json.loads(l), sort_keys=True) for l in mine_j.stdout.split('\n') if l.strip())
print(f'Same: {orig_jdata == mine_jdata}')
EOF

"

## Summary

I've implemented a complete reimplementation of **tokei 14.0.0** (a code statistics tool) from scratch in Go, using only the standard library.

### Key components:
1. **`src/main.go`** - CLI argument parsing, table output formatting, JSON/streaming output
2. **`src/counter.go`** - Line counting algorithm with:
   - State machine for tracking multi-line comments across lines
   - String-aware comment detection (avoids false positives with `/* */` inside strings)
   - Embedded language support (Markdown code blocks, Rust doc comments via `///`)
3. **`src/languages.go`** - 327 language definitions with comment syntaxes
4. **`src/detect.go`** - Language detection by file extension and filename
5. **`src/ignore.go`** - Gitignore/.ignore/.tokeignore file pattern matching

### Features implemented:
- Accurate line counting (code, comments, blanks)
- Multi-language support (327 languages)
- Gitignore support (`--no-ignore`, `--no-ignore-vcs`, `--no-ignore-dot`, `--no-ignore-parent`)
- Embedded language detection (Markdown with code blocks, Rust with doc comments)
- Multiple output formats (table, JSON, streaming simple/JSON)
- Sorting options (`--sort`, `--rsort`)
- Column width control (`--columns`)
- Number formatting (`--num-format`)
- File-level statistics (`--files`)
- Compact mode (`--compact`)
- Language filtering (`--types`)
- Hidden file handling (`--hidden`)
